means: Bright areas bleeding a soft halo into the pixels around them, so a lamp or a lit edge glows outward instead of stopping at its border.
does: As a prompt tag, nothing you can rely on - it is a whole-image property, and this project measured that such clauses re-roll the composition rather than apply the effect. What works is the deterministic path: short.py fx glow is a gblur sigma=18 copy screen-blended back at 0.38 opacity, which IS bloom, and is byte-identical every run. Prefer it. Two warnings when you do: these filters multiply, and glow stacked with hot (contrast 1.10, saturation 1.18, vibrance 0.22) destroyed the climax shot of the first studio-compiled film as an unreadable purple smear - which is why short.py now drops hot to bare contrast 1.08 whenever glow, flash or whiteout is also present.
reach_for_it: for a dream, a memory, a holy or overwhelming light - and reach for the fx, not the tag
used_in: studio/looks/dream.json tags; the glow option of studio/cards/shot_fx.json ('glowing, bloom, soft glow'); short.py fx_chain() glow branch
